maya: Heads-up — we just noticed multiple interface endpoint ENIs in eu-west1b are egressing via the TGW instead of our NAT subnets. Seeing model artifact pulls time out + a TGW egress cost spike. Anyone looking?
Sam L: Which endpoint ID / subnet?
maya: vpce-0f1e2d3c4b (artifact-s3). It's in subnet private-eu-west1b-03. That subnet is associated with RTB rtb-0a1b2 which points 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-0a11b22c. Other private subnets point at nat-0aabbcc.
Aryan: Interface endpoints create ENIs in the subnet you choose — so if that subnet's default route is TGW, outbound to S3 (or any external) will go to TGW. Explains both cost and asymmetry leading to packet drops.
maya: Pod logs show TLS handshake stalls and lots of SYN retries. tcpdump on the ENI shows SYN out, SYN-ACK comes back via the NAT path but then replies take the TGW path -> connection resets. Cost: ~300GB TGW egress in the last hour.
Kevin: Can you paste the route tables?
maya: sure — RTB for the problematic subnet: ```
RouteTable rtb-0a1b2
0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-0a11b22c (assoc: main)
10.10.0.0/16 -> local
```

And the NAT-associated RTB we expected: ```
RouteTable rtb-0c3d4e
0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0aabbcc
10.10.0.0/16 -> local
```
Sam L: So provisioning placed the endpoint ENI into the TGW-associated subnet. You can't move an ENI between subnets. Short-term options: 1) re-create the VPCE in a nat-associated subnet, 2) change that subnet's RTB association (risky), 3) add very specific destination prefixes for the artifact host(s) pointing to the NAT RTB (long-running maintenance burden).
Aryan: Our TF module was using a random private subnet selection function and didn't prefer egress-nat-tagged subnets. I'll open a PR to select by tag (egress:nat=true) and add a validation check that vpce subnet is in the expected list.
maya: Note — security groups won't change routing decisions (SGs are stateful but they don't alter path). We did temporarily throttle artifact pulls and switched apps to mirror endpoints in the datacenter which are on a different route to avoid TGW.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-245 — Interface endpoint egressing via TGW causing failures and cost spike.
Kevin: Action items: 1) script to detect VPCE ENIs in TGW-associated subnets and alert (I'll own). 2) Terraform fix + tests to enforce subnet tagging (Aryan). 3) Runbook for re-creating VPCEs + cost mitigation steps (Sam). 4) TGW egress cost alert at 100GB/hr (Kevin).
Sam L: Agree with order. Anything immediate to stop the bill?
maya: We spun up a temporary NAT in the same AZ and updated the app route to prefer that mirror. It's buying ~30 minutes. Long term we should never land vpce ENIs in TGW subnets.
Aryan: PR link coming in ~30m. Also adding a pre-provision check in the infra CI that fails if any vpce subnet has rtb -> tgw.
Sam L: :thumbsup:
Kevin: I'll add detection + alert and queue the runbook. Thanks everyone.
